strings.adhocempty: Ad hoc task queue is empty
strings.adhocqueueold: Oldest unprocessed task is {$a->age}, which is more than {$a->max}
strings.adhocqueuesize: Ad hoc task queue has {$a} tasks
strings.cannotfindthepathtothecli: Cannot find the path to the PHP CLI executable so task execution aborted. Set the 'Path to PHP CLI' setting in Site administration / Server / System paths.
strings.clearfaildelay_confirm: Are you sure you want to clear the fail delay for task '{$a}'? After clearing the delay, the task will run according to its normal schedule.
strings.confirmdeletetaskwithid: Are you sure you want to delete the task with ID {$a->id}?
strings.crondisabled: Cron is disabled. No new tasks will be started. The system will not operate properly until it is enabled again.
strings.disabled_help: Disabled scheduled tasks are not executed from cron, however they can still be executed manually via the CLI tool.
strings.enablerunnow_desc: Allows administrators to run a single scheduled task immediately, rather than waiting for it to run as scheduled. The feature requires 'Path to PHP CLI' (pathtophp) to be set in System paths. The task runs on the web server, so you may wish to disable this feature to avoid potential performance issues.
strings.privacy:metadata: The Scheduled task configuration plugin does not store any personal data.
strings.resettasktodefaults_help: This will discard any local changes and revert the schedule for this task back to its original settings.
strings.runadhoc_confirm: Tasks will run on the web server and may take some time to complete.
strings.runnow_confirm: Are you sure you want to run this task '{$a}' now? The task will run on the web server and may take some time to complete.
strings.scheduledtaskchangesdisabled: Modifications to the list of scheduled tasks have been prevented in Moodle configuration
strings.slowtask: Task has run for longer than {$a}
strings.taskscheduleday_help: Day of month field for task schedule. The field uses the same format as unix cron. Some examples are: * * Every day * */2 Every 2nd day * 1 The first of every month * 1,15 The first and fifteenth of every month
strings.taskscheduledayofweek_help: Day of week field for task schedule. The field uses the same format as unix cron. Some examples are: * * Every day * 0 Every Sunday * 6 Every Saturday * 1,5 Every Monday and Friday
strings.taskschedulehour_help: Hour field for task schedule. The field uses the same format as unix cron. Some examples are: * * Every hour * */2 Every 2 hours * 2-10 Every hour from 2am until 10am (inclusive) * 2,6,9 2am, 6am and 9am
strings.taskscheduleminute_help: Minute field for task schedule. The field uses the same format as unix cron. Some examples are: * * Every minute * */5 Every 5 minutes * 2-10 Every minute between 2 and 10 past the hour (inclusive) * 2,6,9 2, 6 and 9 minutes past the hour
strings.taskschedulemonth_help: Month field for task schedule. The field uses the same format as unix cron. Some examples are: * * Every month * */2 Every second month * 1 Every January * 1,5 Every January and May
